clue.text: No barnyard fowl, though brought to the barn

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a bird that is not farmyard poultry yet ends up in the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as two words: the ear of wheat is what harvesters carry into the barn, while the one-word bird is a wild songbird, not a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a small wild songbird, no chicken; the second is a grain head gathered at harvest.

clue.text: West side jumpers, outsizes, of unbelievable value

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west
hoppers are things that jump

explanation.surface: Large sweaters from the West sold at unbelievable prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' looks like sweaters but means creatures that hop; the definition covers both senses of the answer: big things and outrageous lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge examples are colloquially called this, and so are barefaced lies nobody could credit.

clue.text: What a bus to be landed with

definitions.text: What a bus to be landed with

parts.words: What a bus to be landed with
parts.note: bus is slang for a motor car, and the landed gentry own a country property, so this is the car for such owners

explanation.walkthrough: 'landed' suggests being burdened, but the landed are property owners; 'bus' is old slang for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-bodied car with a rear door for luggage takes its name from country properties.

indicators.note: in says the loud mark sits inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river, a current in Scotland
FF is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A very loud Welsh voice heard in modern Scottish speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective standing for a noun: a Welshman is nicknamed this, Cymric meaning Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for a Welshman, from the Welsh form of David, fits Cymric (Welsh).

parts.note: split the word: the heart is set in a chest, while the whole word means side by side

explanation.walkthrough: Split as A BREAST, the place where the heart lies; joined, it means level and in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching side by side, level with one another, is being in line.

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at someone's nerve: 'Coo, some neck!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo' and 'neck' look like a cry and cheek; in fact one is the call of a dove of that name and the other is a high rolled collar on a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of that name is a cooing dove; the same word prefixes a high-collared sweater style.

clue.text: But he who surrenders does not have it

definitions.text: But he who surrenders does not have it

parts.words: But he who surrenders does not have it
parts.note: someone who gives in has lost the advantage in the fight

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a position of control, which by definition the side that yields lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Control or advantage over a rival is what the victor holds.

clue.text: He made a go of songwriting

definitions.text: He made a go of songwriting

parts.words: He made a go of songwriting
parts.note: an Italian-born composer whose most famous song is called 'Good-bye', so he made a 'go' song

explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Paolo Tosti wrote the Victorian parlour song 'Good-bye!'; 'made a go' means both succeeded and wrote a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian composer was a celebrated writer of drawing-room songs.

explanation.surface: An announcement that the moment has come for the team to go out and play.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is an hour on the clock; the other is a cricket or football side, which has that many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock hour is one meaning; a cricket or football team of that number is the other.

parts.note: a small sachet of leaves put into a pot to brew a drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Potted' suggests condensed, but it means placed in a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous sachet of leaves is infused in boiling water to make a cuppa.

explanation.surface: A comment that crooked things and dishonest people share a kind of bend.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means warped or askew; read with 'true' as truthfulness, it describes people who have abandoned honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A warped board is bent from its line; a fibber has strayed from veracity.

explanation.surface: A claim that the local police force is a capable outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Latin for 'to be able'; in English it is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to keep order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin verb means to have power to; the English noun is a sheriff's band of deputies.

explanation.surface: A description of a bad-tempered young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusty' suggests grumpy, but here it means having pastry: a small pie. The same word is a pet form of the girl's name Martha or Patricia.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry-covered pie is one sense; a diminutive girl's name is the other.

clue.text: Rose, being a climber, impersonates a prince in Asia

parts.note: Prince Albert, consort of Queen Victoria
taken as written
Asia is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A climbing rose is said to play the part of a royal abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impersonates' is a link: the rose's name is built as the prince, then IN, then E for the East.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a well-known rambling rose variety that climbs walls.

clue.text: Bring up to strength — he helps to

explanation.surface: Advice about reinforcing a team, adding that a certain man helps do it.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means to enlist men to fill a force's numbers; as a noun the new enlistee himself is one who helps bring it up to strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist new members fills out an army; each newly enlisted soldier adds to that number.

clue.text: Suffers — when one takes the subway ?

explanation.surface: A complaint about enduring a trip on the underground.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is endures; read as UNDER GOES, it is what a person does using an underground passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure an ordeal is one sense; to travel below ground is the split reading.

clue.text: Little Greek snakes — clutches of them

parts.note: GR is the short form of Greek
asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Greek snakes, small ones, and their nests of young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' looks like a brood of eggs (fitting 'snakes'), but it is the verb: seizes tightly. 'of them' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch something is to seize and hold it firmly.

parts.note: the head of a college is one who wears academic dress, and capital lent at interest has the same name

explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a college head (cap and gown) and a capital sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A college head bears this title, and a loan's capital sum is called by it too.

parts.note: in Peter Pan, Mr Darling punishes himself by living in the dog's kennel

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Darling is the father in J. M. Barrie's 'Peter Pan'; to be 'in the dog-house' means to be in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in disfavour is described as being in the kennel, which Mr Darling literally was.

clue.text: It puts a citizen in the red ? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the clue says to put a citizen inside the red, but 'Just the opposite' tells us the red goes into the citizen instead

parts.note: CIT is a short form of citizen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about something that sends a person into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' reverses the containment that 'in' first suggests, and also defines: a balance in hand is the opposite of being in the red, which means in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in debit is being in the red; its opposite on a ledger is a positive balance.

clue.text: They are paltry in more ways than two

definitions.text: They are paltry in more ways than two

parts.words: They are paltry in more ways than two
parts.note: Latin for three roads, from the crossroads where idle gossip was exchanged, so it is three ways

explanation.walkthrough: From Latin tri + via, 'three ways': more than two.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty unimportant details are paltry matters.

parts.note: a rod is the tool of angling
a rig is a fisherman's tackle or gear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fishing equipment said to belong to the Spanish hero El Cid.
explanation.walkthrough: El Cid's real first name was Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; 'o'' supplies the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid, the medieval Castilian warlord, was christened with this Spanish given name.

parts.note: a sick person getting better who falls ill again suffers this

explanation.walkthrough: 'well-making' looks like digging a well; it means getting well, recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling back into illness during recovery is a setback.

indicators.note: among says the camping word is placed between the saints

parts.note: to camp is to pitch tents

explanation.surface: Mischief-makers set up their tents among holy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' places CAMPS inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischievous young rogues are little rascals.

parts.note: to drape is to cover
a girl can be referred to as her

explanation.surface: A seductive stranger is told to put a garment over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsider' means one who appears on the outside of a magazine, not a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamorous model photographed for a magazine's front page is pictured on the outside.

explanation.surface: A remark about where a Birmingham football club plays.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a country house; the other is Aston Villa, a football club from Birmingham, often called simply by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country residence is one sense; Aston's Birmingham club is the other.

parts.note: a transparent mineral used for stove windows gives most of the name of this Old Testament prophet

explanation.walkthrough: MICA, the transparent mineral, plus H makes the name of the minor prophet; the question mark flags the loose wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible, with a book of his own.

parts.note: Sandy is a Scotsman, and in Scots the cat's usual prey is pronounced with an oo sound, giving a big deer

explanation.walkthrough: Sandy is a stock name for a Scot; a Scot says 'mouse' with an oo sound, giving a large deer, 'big prey'.
explanation.definitionFit: The large antlered deer of northern forests is big game.

parts.note: mal is French for bad
MO is a short moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: A sorry instant spent while visiting Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place itself: a city found in Sweden, its southern port.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city lies in southern Sweden across the Øresund from Copenhagen.

clue.text: Thou François, after a demon frolic on the spur …

indicators.note: the French word is placed after the demon and the frolic in the answer

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
a romp is a frolic
tu is the French for thou, as a Frenchman like François would say

explanation.surface: Addressing a Frenchman who, after a devilish lark, acts on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the spur' is short for 'on the spur of the moment', meaning unrehearsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unprepared and spontaneous is done without forethought.

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the next word are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Assorted spare parts are hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' turns SPARES into a new order to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant and thinly scattered things are scarce.

clue.text: Early call, padre, our Eleanor called back

parts.note: a padre is a reverend, REV

indicators.note: called back says the girl's name is read from end to start

parts.note: Ellie is a pet form of Eleanor

explanation.surface: A clergyman summons a woman named Eleanor back first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellie is a familiar short form of Eleanor; 'called back' turns her round to follow the padre. The answer is the bugle call that wakes troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle summons that wakes soldiers at dawn is a morning call.
